about: CCwiki's reviewed corrections for deriving relations from the wiki's relations.json. The manifest does not record hardness regimes, scoped notions, refutations or per-direction equivalence classes; these entries supply them until it does. Every entry cites the wiki's own text in `cites`: a page, a section (null for the whole file, frontmatter included) and a quote copied verbatim from the page source, which scripts/derivations_reference.py --check-quotes checks. The prose (evidence, reason or note) is for people. Spec: plans/derivations.md section 2a and plans/relations-followups.md section 2.2; the review is plans/curation-review.md. Read by scripts/derivations_reference.py and by the Swift Derivation type; the corpus test fails if an id here no longer resolves.

It is false — [[AMYY25 - Evasive LWE Attacks, Variants & Obfustopia|AMYY25]]

refuted.text: SIDH is broken classically in polynomial time (CD22).

cites.quote: In 2022, a classical polynomial-time attack was discovered that completely breaks SIDH — [[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]]
the conjecture is false: SIDH is broken classically — [[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]]

refuted.text: SSDDH is the decisional variant of SIDH, which CD22 breaks classically in polynomial time from the same transcript.

cites.quote: The _supersingular decision Diffie-Hellman (SSDDH)_ problem is to distinguish the shared curve $E_{AB}$ from the quotient of $E$ by an independent pair of kernel points, given the SIDH transcript
A classical polynomial-time attack on SIDH, using Kani's theorem and the auxiliary torsion-point information — [[CD22 - An efficient key recovery attack on SIDH|CD22]]
The attack breaks SIDH completely

settings.text: A corruption setting, not an assumption: MPC with t < n/2 exists unconditionally given broadcast (RB89).

cites.quote: When fewer than a threshold fraction of parties are corrupt, information-theoretic (unconditional) security is achievable.
For $t < n/2$, statistical security against malicious adversaries is achievable with broadcast — [[RB89 - Verifiable Secret Sharing and Multiparty Protocols with Honest Majority|RB89]].

settings.text: A corruption setting, not an assumption: MPC with t < n/3 exists unconditionally (BGW88).

cites.quote: When fewer than a threshold fraction of parties are corrupt, information-theoretic (unconditional) security is achievable.

red-isis-inhomogeneous-sis-to-sis.note: SIS => ISIS is immediate; ISIS => SIS holds only under conditions on the column count and norm bound (requires entry below).

The other, ISIS hardness implying SIS hardness (solving ISIS with a SIS oracle), holds only under conditions on the column count and norm bound.

red-linear-secret-sharing-schemes-lsss-t.note: KW93 and Bei96: both directions are size-preserving translations.

cites.quote: an MSP of size $m$ computing an access structure $\Gamma$ yields an LSSS for $\Gamma$ with total share size $m$ field elements, and every LSSS for $\Gamma$ induces an MSP of the same size computing $\Gamma$
The equivalence is an unconditional linear-algebraic correspondence, with no assumption or adversary to use as an oracle.

cites.quote: [[learning-with-errors#degree-1-module-lwe|Module LWE]] over the degree-1 ring $R = \ZZ$ at module rank $n$ is [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] in dimension $n$ with the same modulus, error distribution and number of samples, so each is hard if and only if the other is

red-rabin-ot-to-ot.note: Cre87: each direction is an information-theoretic protocol.

cites.quote: each is realized from the other by an information-theoretically secure protocol making polynomially many calls
Each direction calls the given OT only as a subprotocol on locally chosen inputs, and its security is information-theoretic given ideal calls, so the simulators use the adversary only as a black box.

red-rsa-to-fac-dlo24.note: RSA => FAC is trivial in the standard model, FAC => RSA is DLO24's generic-ring theorem; the recorded model 'other' is kept for both, which only under-claims the trivial direction.

cites.quote: Against generic ring algorithms, which access $\ZZ_n$ only through ring operations and equality tests, computing $e$-th roots modulo $n$ ([[rsa-assumption|RSA]]) is equivalent to [[factoring|factoring]] $n$
The converse holds unconditionally: the factorization of $n$ gives $\phi(n)$ and hence $d \equiv e^{-1} \pmod{\phi(n)}$
The theorem is proved in the generic ring model with preprocessing, which is none of the named models and differs from the generic group model.
